card.title: Essay 5 — Scientific Research is a Token of Humankind's Survival (Vladimir Keilis-Borok)

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: ## The essay at a glance "Scientific Research Is a Token of Humankind's Survival" by Vladimir Keilis-Borok is a scientist's public plea: research, it argues, is not a luxury for the rich or a hobby for the curious but the mechanism by which humanity predicts and survives its disasters.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Research is humankind's survival tool — curiosity now prevents catastrophe later.
Argument structure: small findings accumulate into civilisational protection.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Trick 3: Funding argument: basic research looks useless today but pays off tomorrow — the delayed-return logic is the essay's hardest point; explain it with one example.  ·  ## The themes worth an essay **Science as survival** — the central theme: research is civilisation's defence against both natural and self-made disasters. **The economics of prevention** — funding research is cheaper than funding recovery; the theme argues against the habit of cutting science in calm years.…

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: ## The title, defended "Scientific Research Is a Token of Humankind's Survival" states its claim as an equation, and the confidence is the point. The defence a candidate should write: a *token* is evidence and pledge at once — research is both the proof that humanity can outthink its dangers and the payment that guarantees it.…  ·  ## NEB short answers, solved **Q. Why does the writer call scientific research a token of humankind's survival? (2 marks)** A. Because research is the mechanism by which humanity predicts and survives its disasters — earthquakes, floods, disease, famine. It is both evidence of our capacity to outthink nature and the pledge that we will: without it, survival is luck; with it, survival is policy. **Q.…

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Why does the writer call research a token of survival? (2 marks) — every human crisis has been answered by scientific research; future threats need it too.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ## NEB long answers, solved **Q. "Research is insurance paid in calm years." Explain this idea from the essay. (8 marks)** A model answer unpacks the analogy: premiums are the steady, unglamorous funding of research during quiet decades; the payout is prediction and preparation when the disaster arrives.…  ·  **‘Scientific Research...’ — the case for research (classified)** | Argument | Explanation | Exam use | |---|---|---| | Civilisation’s insurance | Knowledge prepared before crisis arrives | 2-m: state the metaphor | | Earthquake example | Prediction research saves lives | 4-m: develop with detail | | Young scientists needed | Talent is the raw material of survival | 8-m: concluding appeal | |…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## The argument, step by step The essay opens on the planet's violence: earthquakes, floods, eruptions and the disasters humanity adds of its own. Against this, the writer sets the one instrument that has ever reduced their cost — systematic research: the earth sciences that locate fault lines and assess hazards, the medicine that defeats diseases, the engineering that keeps cities standing.…  ·  ## The devices, with evidence - **Cost-benefit argument** — the essay's persuasive spine: research priced against catastrophe, a comparison no accountant can refuse. - **Analogy** — research as insurance: premiums paid in calm years, payouts in crisis; the analogy translates seismology into civic arithmetic.…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 1: Thesis: humanity survives because research keeps solving new threats — science as insurance; state the thesis in one line.  ·  Trick 2: The seismologist's examples: earthquake prediction, medicine, energy — pick two of his examples to show 'research = survival'.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. Why should society fund 'useless' basic research? (2 marks) — today's curiosity becomes tomorrow's cure; give one example (e.g. earthquake studies).
